    • It has been revealed that staying properly hydrated has many health benefits—it promotes cardiovascular health, enhances skin elasticity, and eliminates waste from the body—and using a countertop water filter is an easy way to get safe, clean drinking water right in your kitchen.
    • To help you find the right one for your water quality and household needs, we spent 2 weeks testing seven of the most popular models on the market today.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We may earn revenue from the products available on this page and participate in affiliate programs. Learn More ›.

    It has been revealed that staying properly hydrated has many health benefits—it promotes cardiovascular health, enhances skin elasticity, and eliminates waste from the body—and using a countertop water filter is an easy way to get safe, clean drinking water right in your kitchen. These user-friendly appliances either sit on your counter or attach to your faucet, removing common contaminants like chemicals, heavy metals, and bacteria without requiring permanent plumbing. Not only that, they help reduce the plastic waste associated with buying bottled water.

    To help you find the right one for your water quality and household needs, we spent 2 weeks testing seven of the most popular models on the market today. Based on our results, we chose the Bluevua Countertop Reverse Osmosis Water Filter System as our favorite for its easy setup, third-party contaminant removal certifications, long filter life, and remineralization stage that restores beneficial minerals for a smooth taste. Read on for our detailed reviews of the best countertop water filters and to learn what matters most when choosing the one for you.

    Bottom line: Countertop water filters offer a convenient way to access clean, safe drinking water, with options to suit various needs and budgets.

    According to recent reports, the products below represent the “best in show” in home water filtration. These top picks were chosen based on quality, functionality, and reputation.

    It has been revealed that this was the first unit we tested, and it ended up being our favorite. Installation was incredibly easy—just fill the removable water reservoir, plug the unit in, and press start. As with any reverse osmosis (RO) water filter system, you’ll also want to discard the first two tanks of water as part of flushing the newly introduced filters, but after that, you’ll get nothing but pure, great-tasting water. In fact, we thought the water from this model was some of the best, due to its comprehensive filtration as well as the fact that it undergoes a remineralization stage to add calcium and magnesium back in for a super smooth taste.

    In a recent development, another favorite feature was the built-in LCD screen that highlights total dissolved solids (TDS) before and after each cycle, giving us visible proof that its NSF- and WQA-certified filtration system was actively removing contaminants. That display also shows when it’s time to replace each of the four filters (they all have relatively long lifespans of 12 to 24 months), and changing them is easy since they twist right out (there’s also a reset button for each one to patch its filter life indicator). We also really liked that it dispenses directly into a glass carafe that maintains the water’s crisp taste and fits easily into our fridge. The Bluevua isn’t the least expensive model on this list, but for an RO unit with remineralization, it provides an excellent value—provided you have the counter space for it.

    Sources indicate that what our tester says: “I’ve been drinking alkaline water for years, and I greatly prefer it to the flat taste of reverse osmosis water. Since the Bluevua gives me both, it’s my new favorite water filter!”—Michelle Larson, Product Reviews tester and writer.

    Get the Bluevua countertop water filter at Amazon or Bluevua.

    As another RO system with remineralization, this Waterdrop gave the Bluevua a real run for its money. We loved the slightly lower price point and slightly smaller footprint, but it ultimately came in second because it (unlike several others in the brand’s lineup) is yet to hold any third-party certifications—though we hope it’s just a matter of time since this model is relatively fresh. Like the Bluevua, it features a digital display that shows TDS levels before and after filtration, and like every unit we tested, it passed our manual water-quality tests with flying colors.

    Industry observers note that while traditional RO systems can be a bit of a pain to install, setting up this countertop reverse osmosis filter is as easy as plugging it in, filling the reservoir, and throwing away the first couple of pitchers. You can filter water directly into your own container or the included 32-ounce water tank, which means you can chill one batch in the fridge while still having the option to grab a quick room-temp cup. And since the seven-stage filtration process takes place inside a single composite cartridge, maintenance is incredibly easy even if it’s a little more frequent (there’s a filter life indicator, and Waterdrop indicates to expect replacement about every 12 months). Considering its budget-friendly price point, sleek design, and delicious water, there are days we might actually vote this model number one.

    Sources indicate that what our tester indicates: “I’ve actually tested a couple of Waterdrop water filters now, and each has been a pleasure to use. The firm consistently prioritizes user-friendliness, and because this RO model also adds minerals back in, the final product tastes excellent.”—Michelle Larson, Product Reviews tester and writer.

    Get the Waterdrop countertop water filter at Amazon or Waterdrop.

    If you want reliable multi-stage water filtration without giving up counter space or worrying about cords, this simple pitcher filter from Epic could be ideal. The simple gravity-fed setup is compact enough for small apartments and dorm rooms and user-friendly enough for anyone seeking straightforward pour-in, pour-out convenience. Despite its small footprint, it offers as much or more capacity than many options on this list, storing easily on the counter or in the fridge.

    In terms of technology, the Pure XP uses a nanofiber and carbon-block core to reduce over 70 common drinking water contaminants—including heavy metals, forever chemicals (PFAS), microplastics, and parasites—while retaining naturally occurring trace minerals. It holds an array of third-party certifications and uses BPA- and BPS-free materials to avoid introducing any chemicals back in. Cleaning and maintenance are easy: simply hand wash the pitcher and swap out the inner cartridge every 3 to 4 months (the outer portion is reusable to cut down on plastic waste). This means you may end up spending a little more on replacement filters than you would with some other systems, but given the very reasonable purchase price, you’re definitely still getting a good deal.

    Recent findings suggest that what our tester claims: “If you’re looking for a classic Brita-style pitcher but want to be sure it’s pulling out all the gunk you don’t want, this is it. It’s also incredibly easy to use, and the water tastes great!”—Michelle Larson, Product Reviews tester and writer.

    Get the Epic Water Filters countertop water filter at Amazon or Epic Water Filters.

    According to recent reports, setting up the Waterdrop M6CG couldn’t have been much easier. After filling the rear reservoir and getting everything running, we were impressed by how neatly the unit fit into a coffee and tea station despite giving you both hot and cold filtered water. We initially wished there was an option to connect it directly to a water line, but since an RO system also needs somewhere to send wastewater, the refillable tank setup will probably be more practical for most kitchens anyway. Most importantly, the filtered water tasted noticeably better than our unfiltered tap water, and the hot-water function gave us water that was more than hot enough for tea without waiting for a kettle.

    According to recent reports, our biggest complaint is dispensing speed. Compared with a refrigerator dispenser or traditional water cooler, the Waterdrop feels extremely slow, particularly when filling a mug with hot water. The touchscreen is attractive and generally intuitive, but things get more cumbersome when you want a quantity that isn’t one of the presets. Dialing in our preferred 10-ounce serving took more tapping than expected, though thankfully the machine lets you save custom settings as favorites.

    In a recent development, we also liked the glass carafe attached to the machine, which fills from the bottom and keeps room-temperature filtered water ready to grab at any time (it also looks and feels super premium). The system provides helpful reminders when the reservoir needs attention, although they can occasionally feel unnecessary, such as reminding us to refill or empty the tank while we’re already removing it to do exactly that. Overall, this is a capable, attractive RO dispenser that produces great-tasting water and useful hot and cold options. We just wish its dispensing speed and interface felt a little more polished given the premium price.

    Get the Waterdrop M6CG countertop water filter at Amazon, Target, Best Buy, or Walmart.

    Industry observers note that comparing the certifications of all the filtered water systems in this guide had its confusing moments, but as we worked, we learned that the AquaTru Classic RO system is one of the most highly certified units on the market. With its comprehensive four-stage design, it can trap a total of 84 contaminants, including everything from coarse sediment and chlorine to heavy metals, fluoride, microplastics, and forever chemicals (PFAS). And with a 2.84-liter clean water tank, it also holds more purified water than any other reverse osmosis system on our list.

    Recent findings suggest that because the filters last anywhere from 6 months to 2 years (depending on which of the three filters you’re replacing), maintenance is also minimal, especially compared to standard pitcher filters. Like all RO systems, though, it also takes up more counter space than basic units. Ultimately, its higher upfront cost and lack of remineralization kept it out of the top spot, but those with high-capacity demands who love everything else about it will be happy to hear AquaTru sells replacement filters with minerals—making cost the only real hurdle.

    Get the AquaTru countertop water filter at Amazon, The Home Depot, Best Buy, or AquaTru.

    One of the biggest downsides of faucet-connected systems is that their hoses can easily get in the way of other sink-related tasks, like washing your hands or doing the dishes. They also create a cluttered look, which Brondell seems to acknowledge, as the brand doesn’t show any photos of this model actually hooked up to a faucet. However, if you purchase an inexpensive T-valve and don’t mind drilling a small hole in your countertop, you can run that hose under your sink for a totally seamless look. And because this pick allows for virtually instant filtration, you get purified water on demand no matter which setup you choose.

    Performance-wise, the Cypress countertop filter uses a three-stage system that combines a sediment filter, a patented Nanotrap filter, and a carbon block to pull out chlorine, microplastics, VOCs, and fine particles. Water dispenses instantly at the press of a button with zero wastewater generated, making it faster than gravity pitchers and more efficient than reverse osmosis setups. It also has a slim footprint that takes up minimal countertop space, though because it’s only about 10 inches tall, it’s hard to fill tall bottles or large pots (we had to reposition it over the sink to do so during testing). Still, it comes at a great price for a WQA Gold Seal-certified unit with filters that last 6 months to 1 year, making it a good water filter for homes with high-volume needs.

    Get the Brondell countertop water filter at Amazon or Brondell.

    According to recent reports, there’s no denying the popularity of the Substantial Berkey: its stainless steel construction and massive 8.5-liter capacity have made it a staple for large households and off-grid enthusiasts. Because it relies strictly on gravity and its proprietary Black Berkey filters, it functions entirely without electricity, plumbing, or tap pressure—you simply pour water into the top chamber and let it drip down. It also has an extremely long filter lifespan of up to 6,000 gallons per pair, meaning you won’t be constantly buying replacements.

    However, its popularity comes with a couple of drawbacks. Despite the hefty price tag, Berkey lacks any official certifications, relying instead on independent lab testing. And like all gravity systems, it’s also quite bulky, standing almost 20 inches tall with no option for fridge storage. Also, because it relies on gravity, the filtration rate is quite slow—we got into the habit of filling the top reservoir a couple of times a day so it had several hours to make its way to the bottom. Still, with no gauge of any sort, we never really had any idea how much water was even in the bottom chamber. All that aside, Berkey has an almost cult-like following, and the durable stainless steel water filter body and straightforward operation are likely why.

    Get the Substantial Berkey countertop water filter at Amazon.

    To find a selection of the best countertop water filters for home use, we began by evaluating dozens of popular models, focusing on ease of installation and use, filtration claims, capacity, and price.

    After selecting seven units for testing, we performed the same set of steps with each, starting with installation. Next, we performed water quality tests before and after filtration to measure contaminant reduction, followed by blind taste tests to rate flavor and odor. We measured flow rate by timing how long each unit took to process or dispense a quart of water, assessed how easy each unit was to clean and change filters on, and rated general convenience of extra features like filter life indicators and removable pitchers.

    We used each model for a minimum of 2 days to get a feel for how much we liked them overall, and for the faucet-connected models, to see whether they got in the way during regular tasks like washing hands or dishes.

    Industry observers note that the best countertop water filtration system for your home will depend on the quality concerns you want to address, how much filtered water your household uses, and how much daily upkeep you’re willing to take on. It’s smart to request a copy of your local utility’s Consumer Confidence Report or use a home water test kit, then compare potential systems’ filtration claims, capacity, footprint, and replacement-filter cost.

    Recent findings suggest that countertop water filters generally fall into two broad categories: reservoir-based systems and faucet-connected systems. Reservoir models don’t connect to your plumbing at all, while faucet-connected models attach to a standard faucet or use a diverter valve under your sink.

    In a recent development, reservoir systems hold untreated water in one tank or chamber and deliver clean water into another after it passes through the system’s filter(s). The simplest versions are water pitchers like the Epic Water Filters Pure XP Water Filter Pitcher or gravity systems like the Substantial Berkey Gravity-Fed Water Filter. Since they don’t connect to your faucet, they’re great for apartments, dorms, RVs, and kitchens with incompatible faucets.

    Countertop reverse osmosis systems also use a refillable reservoir, but rather than relying on gravity, they have an internal pump that forces the water through their filters before delivering it to a pitcher or your glass. RO systems have the added benefit of reducing dissolved solids in untreated water, but that includes beneficial minerals like calcium and magnesium and also creates wastewater that must be dumped (or used for things like cleaning or watering plants).

    According to recent reports, faucet-connected filters either attach directly to your faucet or connect via a hose and diverter valve. When the diverter is switched to the filtration setting, tap water filters through the unit on demand and into your glass, bottle, or pot. When the diverter is off, water flows straight out of the tap as normal.

    Two major things to consider regarding faucet-connected systems are faucet compatibility and installation. Most aren’t compatible with pull-down, pull-out, spray, sensor-operated, or nonstandard faucets, and many also have small hoses that connect the faucet to the machine, which takes up a bit of space and can look cluttered. Some allow you to run the hoses from the machine to the plumbing under your sink, but that will require an adapter and a hole in the counter for the cords to route through.

    While it can be tempting to choose the purification system for water that has the longest list of contaminants removed, it’s ultimately more vital to pair the system you choose with what you’re actually trying to filter out of your water.

    Recent findings suggest that most of the best water filters have activated-carbon filters that remove unpleasant tastes and odors and may reduce other chemicals or particulates. Some systems add sediment filtration or specialty media to target things like lead, fluoride, or PFAS compounds. Since performance varies by model, always check the manufacturer’s claims rather than assuming they all work the same.

    According to recent reports, reverse-osmosis systems use a membrane designed to reduce dissolved solids, which means they generally remove more contaminants than basic filtration systems. However, they can also reduce beneficial minerals, which is why some manufacturers are now adding a remineralization stage to return the filtered water to a more alkaline state.

    Many of the units on this list carry third-party certification to verify tested performance beyond manufacturer claims. NSF International’s drinking-water treatment standards are the most commonly used, although you may also see mentions of accredited organizations like IAPMO R&T or WQA. While our tests using the Varify Complete Drinking Water Test Kit for this guide backed up the manufacturers’ claims, it’s still a good idea to prioritize products that carry filter certifications and look up which contaminants the product is certified to remove.

    Sources indicate that then, match the certification to your specific concern. For example, if lead reduction is your main goal, you’ll want a model with NSF 53 and 58 listings.

    It has been revealed that capacity has two meanings: how much water a filter can treat before replacement and how much filtered water the unit can provide at once. For our purposes, we’re defining it as how much it can filter at once, as we discuss filter life in the next section.

    Since reservoir models’ ready-to-drink supply is based on the size of their clean-water chambers, larger households or those with greater needs will want to prioritize a model that holds multiple liters or gallons. Faucet-connected models can also be a good choice in those situations, as they can deliver clean water continuously as long as the tap is on.

    Flow rate—how promptly the filter provides clean drinking water—is another notable consideration. However, many manufacturers don’t list this information, and it can also vary depending on water pressure, source-water quality, temperature, and cartridge age. If this is a major concern, you may want to reach out to manufacturers directly or read online reviews for mentions of filtration speed.

    Every countertop drinking water filter system requires filter replacement on a set schedule, which means the true cost of ownership ends up being more than what you paid for it. When choosing between systems, compare the number of filters, their individual projected filter capacity, and each one’s replacement cost.

    According to recent reports, A basic pitcher may use a single cartridge that’s easy to change but needs more frequent replacement, while a multistage RO unit may have multiple filters that each have different change intervals and prices. While systems with filter-life indicators can make it much easier to know when it’s time to swap them, if your unit is noticeably slower or isn’t providing the same quality, you may still need to change filters even if it isn’t technically time.

    Countertop water filters are generally pretty straightforward, but the following answers to commonly asked questions can answer any lingering queries you may have.

    In a recent development, water filters work by using a filtration mechanism to capture organisms and chemicals that lead to unsafe or cloudy water. A fabricated surface traps the larger contaminants, while a compound like activated carbon works as a magnet to trap smaller contaminants.

    According to recent reports, installation depends on the type: A faucet-connected filtration system typically attaches to a compatible faucet aerator or diverter valve, while dispenser, pitcher, gravity-fed, and countertop RO models generally only require rinsing the parts, installing the filters, and filling the reservoir. Always follow the manufacturer’s instructions, especially for RO units that may also require an initial flush cycle.

    No, countertop water purification filters do not work with every type of kitchen faucet. Specifically, more modern designs and detachable faucets with spray nozzles may be incompatible with faucet-connected countertop water filters.

    Most filters can remove chlorine, fluoride, bacteria, and parasites. To know exactly which contaminants a specific filter can remove or reduce, consult the manufacturer’s information regarding filter certification.

    Yes, bacteria can grow in a countertop filter, so it’s a good idea to flush the faucet for about 20 seconds after turning on the water and then for an additional 5 to 10 seconds to filter and flush out any bacteria that may be lingering in the faucet.

    Sources indicate that yes, countertop reverse osmosis systems are worth it for households seeking to remove dissolved contaminants like lead and fluoride and who prefer a plumbing-free setup. However, they generally cost more and require more maintenance than pitchers or carbon-filter-only units, so they’re best when your water test or local report identifies concerns simpler filters can’t address.

    Sources indicate that filter replacement timing varies by system and filter type, so it’s best to follow the manufacturer’s schedule for your specific system. Generally speaking, pitcher and faucet units may need latest filters every few months, while countertop RO filters and membranes may last anywhere from 6 months to 2 years. You may need to replace filters sooner if the flow slows noticeably or your water develops an unusual taste or odor.

    In a recent development, michelle Larson has been a writer and editor for more than 10 years in the fields of health, business, and the home. Because she’d rather spend a little more up front than buy a tool or appliance twice, she strongly believes in the power of testing for finding quality items that are meant to last.

    John Yoo on "Leaving a [University of] California that Rejects the West"

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (542 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Reason

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that professor John Yoo is leaving the law school at the University of California at Berkeley to join the School of Civic Leadership at the University of Texas at Austin.
    • Given the attention his move has received, Yoo has written an op-ed for the New York Post explaining his decision to choose Texas, and disputing any suggestion that he was driven out of Berkeley.
    • I'm leaving not because I feel driven out by Berkeley — anything but.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that professor John Yoo is leaving the law school at the University of California at Berkeley to join the School of Civic Leadership at the University of Texas at Austin. As I noted here, his departure means there will not be a single right-leaning professor teaching public law subjects at Berkeley--and no more than a handful (if that) at all of the UC schools combined.

    Given the attention his move has received, Yoo has written an op-ed for the New York Post explaining his decision to choose Texas, and disputing any suggestion that he was driven out of Berkeley.

    I'm leaving not because I feel driven out by Berkeley — anything but.

    In my three decades there I've enjoyed working, on an individual level, with spirited, ambitious students and challenging, innovative scholars.

    I'm moving because Berkeley, like its peers, has declined from a daring, risk-taking center of higher learning to one that wallows contentedly in a monoculture of liberalism.

    Yoo states the school has been obsessed with ethnic diversity while disregarding viewpoint diversity, and that this has eroded the institution's commitment to free speech and created an environment in which anti-semitism has taken root.

    I've watched students and the usual agitators disrupt debates on affirmative action, spark pitched fights on Sproul Plaza and try to shout down distinguished scholars and thinkers (home of the Free Speech Movement, indeed).

    Tolerance of such shenanigans was matched by intolerance of conservative or libertarian views on the faculty.

    Berkeley has consistently rejected conservative scholars, no matter how well-qualified, well-published or widely cited. . . .

    Sources indicate that one famous member of a revered Berkeley humanities department (always ranked among the nation's top three) once told me directly that he would never hire a conservative. . . .

    Most student groups at Berkeley Law now boycott any event with a speaker who believes in Israel's right to exist.

    For the first time in my 33 years at Berkeley I witnessed a heckler's veto, as protesters prevented a member of the Israeli Knesset from speaking — and top university officials stood idly by.

    Students posted flyers depicting the dean of the law school — a liberal scholar with whom I rarely agree — feasting on human beings, then physically invaded his home while he hosted members of the graduating class, simply because he is Jewish.

    Yoo argues that great universities should refocus their teaching on Western Civilization, so that the nation does not lose sight of the ideals upon which it was founded and the principles that provide the foundation for western prosperity.

    The emergence of human reason in Greece and religious revelation in Jerusalem produced the free markets, natural rights, rule of law and democratic self-government that have made our astounding prosperity and power possible.

    It has been revealed that these ideals run directly counter to the poison running rampant on our campuses. . . .

    Texas wants to restore Western civilization and the great books to the center of its curriculum — not to blindly agree with the past, but to understand and debate it.

    I'm eager to join the Texans who want to defend free speech and thought, and to leave behind a California that rejects the West.

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (734 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Bobvila ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Dupray Bloom Review: A HEPA Air Purifier Worth Putting on Display

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (734 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bobvila

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, we may earn revenue from the products available on this page and participate in affiliate programs.
    • I’ve tested a lot of air purifiers, and most look like appliances I’d rather tuck out of sight in a corner.
    • Absolutely, and that’s what makes the Bloom so appealing.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, we may earn revenue from the products available on this page and participate in affiliate programs. Learn More ›.

    I’ve tested a lot of air purifiers, and most look like appliances I’d rather tuck out of sight in a corner. The Dupray Bloom Air Purifier is different. It combines a HEPA air purifier with a removable planter, turning something purely functional into a decorative accent. I planted a small fiddle-leaf fig in mine, and I love how it looks in the room. But I also wanted to know whether the Bloom’s unusual design would interfere with its primary job of filtering the air.

    Absolutely, and that’s what makes the Bloom so appealing. The top features a removable planting pot with a root tray that helps keep roots above excess water. I chose a small fiddle-leaf fig, and once it was planted, the Bloom looked more like a decorative planter than an air-cleaning appliance.

    There is one thing I’d caution buyers about: The planter doesn’t have drainage holes. The root tray provides some separation from standing water, but it isn’t a substitute for proper watering. I’d recommend using an olla, a small porous automatic watering vessel that slowly releases moisture into the soil. It’s a good option for keeping the plant watered without repeatedly pouring water into a pot that can’t drain.

    Recent findings suggest that I also appreciated that the planter lifts completely out. That means I can move the plant for maintenance or repotting without having to move the entire purifier. And when it’s time to replace the round HEPA filter, I can remove the planter, turn the unit over, and access the filter from the bottom.

    Behind its decorative design, the Bloom is a serious air purifier. It uses an H13 HEPA filter with activated carbon to capture airborne particles, including dust, pollen, and pet dander, while helping reduce odors. Dupray rates it as capable of capturing 99.97 percent of particles as small as 0.1 micron.

    Recent findings suggest that one feature I particularly liked was the stretchy fabric prefilter. It slips snugly over the purifier’s base, creating a smooth, modern appearance while catching larger airborne particles before they reach the HEPA filter. It’s washable, too, and Dupray offers replacement prefilters in different colors.

    Recent findings suggest that the Bloom also has an AutoDetect mode that monitors air quality and adjusts the fan speed. There are three manual fan settings, along with a sleep mode for quieter operation. Dupray rates its lowest noise level at just 24 decibels, making it suitable for bedrooms and other living spaces where a loud fan would be distracting.

    It has been revealed that it’s remarkably simple. The removable planter makes the HEPA filter accessible, and the fabric prefilter stretches on and off without clips or complicated fasteners.

    Recent findings suggest that another smart touch is the universal power adapter. It comes with interchangeable plug configurations for the U.S., U.K., and Europe. That’s not something I typically see included with an air purifier.

    Recent findings suggest that my only complaint—and it’s minor—is the digital control display. The symbols for Auto, Sleep, and the fan-speed bars looked slightly blurry to me. I could still identify them and operate the purifier, but a sharper display would have been easier to read. Or I might need a newly introduced prescription for glasses.

    Industry observers note that at $249.99, the Bloom isn’t the cheapest way to get HEPA filtration, but its design sets it apart from the usual boxy models. It’s particularly appealing for living rooms, bedrooms, and home offices where an ordinary air purifier might detract from the decor.

    Dupray advertises coverage up to 1,517 square feet, but that’s based on just one air change per hour. For more frequent air cleaning, it’s rated to cover 316 square feet at 4.8 air changes per hour. I’d use that smaller figure when choosing where to place it.

    The Bloom also offers an optional wood tabletop model for anyone who prefers an accent table instead of a planter.

    I love having a living plant incorporated into an appliance I’d otherwise try to hide. The Bloom is one of the few air purifiers I’ve tested that I’d happily put on display.

    Breaking: Second Amendment Roundup: AR-15 Film Redux.

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (777 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Reason

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Smith released his upcoming 85-minute film discussing the operations and mechanics of modern firearms, including semiautomatic rifles such as the popular AR-15 rifle.
    • It has been revealed that that federal judges are now reviewing Internet videos to learn about firearms is hardly surprising.
    • Industry observers note that as I previously wrote, I had the pleasure of introducing the "AR-15 Primer" film.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Last week, Professor Mark W. Smith released his upcoming 85-minute film discussing the operations and mechanics of modern firearms, including semiautomatic rifles such as the popular AR-15 rifle. The film, titled "Firearms and the AR-15 Rifle: A Primer for the Bench and Bar," can be found on YouTube here and on Rumble. It has already been viewed over 23,000 times since its release only days ago. The film is broken down into 25 segments so a viewer can jump from topic to topic.

    It has been revealed that that federal judges are now reviewing Internet videos to learn about firearms is hardly surprising. A few weeks ago Judge Doris Pryor of the Seventh Circuit made reference to this during oral argument in a constitutional fight over the legality of Illinois's suppressor ban. In the consolidated cases of Anderson v. Raoul and Morse v. Raoul, argued October 28, 2026, she acknowledged that she has watched videos in preparing for oral argument. The oral argument audio recording is here with Judge Pryor's comment at the 25:04-25:23 mark.

    Industry observers note that as I previously wrote, I had the pleasure of introducing the "AR-15 Primer" film. From there, Rick Vasquez (a former ATF firearm technician and U.S. Marine ordnance officer) takes the spotlight explaining the mechanical operation of today's AR-15 rifle and its typical features.

    Industry observers note that but there is another crucial aspect of the film that is worth noting. And that is the impressive animations found within the film that help educate legal professionals and the general public about the internal and related operations of the AR-15 (and most modern semi-automatic rifles).

    The animations found throughout the film are informative for those learning about firearm mechanics. Here are a few of the noteworthy ones:.

    There is an excellent 2-minute animation illustrating how gas-operated semiautomatic rifles internally deploy the rapidly-expanding gases from the firing of a shot to do two things: first, to send a projectile (the bullet) down the barrel and, second, to prepare the rifle to fire the next round of ammunition. This is called autoloading. This dual use of the gases from firing a single shot is generally not understood or appreciated by those newly introduced to firearms technology, but the film's animation makes it clear. This animation also clarifies that autoloading does not mean automatic fire (like one sees with a M16 machine gun). The animation can be seen at the 14:58 to 17:58 mark of the film.

    The film also does a nice job demonstrating the physical reality of recoil by illustrating how the features of an AR-15 like the straight line stock, the buffer spring/buffer tube, and the muzzle brake help to minimize recoil allowing for a more comfortable and effective shooting experience. The 28:09 to 28:22 mark has a nice illustration of the straight-line stock while the 28:28 to 28:59 mark illustrates the role of the buffer and buffer spring in minimizing uncomfortable recoil. The 27:59 to 28:07 mark demonstrates an animation illustrating what constitutes recoil from the firing of a rifle.

    Sources indicate that the film also effectively uses animation to illustrate the difference between scopes, red dot optics, and iron sights. A scope magnifies the target making it appear closer than it really is; a red dot optic helps the user aim the rifle using an electronic dot without magnification; and iron sights entail aligning a front post with a rear sight. The 1:00:53 to 1:01:18 mark illustrates these differences.

    Animation also helps viewers understand that the barrel of a semiautomatic rifle gets hot when the rifle is fired due to the internal gas explosion that results from firing a round. The film's animation reveals the rifle barrel heating up and demonstrates the value of handguards (often called "barrel shrouds" in legislation) to protect the user of the rifle. The 46:24 to 46:33 mark illustrates a barrel heating up as the rifle is shot.

    The film's use of animations to explain the difference between a bullet and a cartridge is also worth mentioning. Lawyers (and even some judges) use those terms interchangeably, but they mean very different things. The 1:10:12 to 1:11:08 mark illustrates the four components (primer, gun power, case and bullet) of a modern ammunition cartridge.

    Industry observers note that it has been said that the late President Harry Truman embraced the thought, "I am from Missouri so you have to show me." Well, Professor Smith's fresh film on firearm mechanics works hard to "show" (through animations, illustrations and images) the internal mechanics and features of AR-15 semiautomatic rifles. And I suspect the bench and the bar will be the better for it.

    Sources indicate that police sirens can sound very different, from a slow wail to a rapid yelp. Here’s why officers switch tones and what drivers should do.

    In a recent development, everyone recognizes an emergency siren. Or do they?

    Officers can choose different tones to make their vehicles easier to notice on busy streets or open roads. Some departments also use certain sounds for special warnings. With electronic siren systems offering several options, drivers might hear multiple tones during a single emergency response.

    Learn what the common sounds mean, why officers switch between them, whether different tones signal different emergencies, and how drivers should react.

    It has been revealed that different police siren sounds serve different purposes, but they don’t necessarily indicate specific emergencies. Officers often switch tones based on traffic conditions or to get drivers’ attention. A faster siren doesn’t always mean a more serious emergency.

    The most common police siren sounds include:.

    Modern police vehicles typically use electronic sirens that allow officers to switch between these sounds. Older mechanical sirens use a spinning mechanism to produce a traditional wail.

    Recent findings suggest that officers also adjust their sirens based on traffic conditions. Faster tones can help get drivers’ attention in heavy traffic, while a slower wail may work on quieter roads. Departments set their own policies for siren use, so there isn’t one standard sound for daytime or nighttime driving.

    According to recent reports, regardless of the siren sound, drivers should respond the same way when an emergency vehicle approaches. Drivers should check their mirrors, signal, and safely pull toward the right side of the road to let the police vehicle pass. They should avoid sudden braking or stopping in an intersection.

    According to recent reports, anyone already in an intersection should continue through before pulling over. Drivers waiting at a red light shouldn’t enter the intersection unless an officer directs them to do so. After the police vehicle passes, drivers should check for other emergency vehicles before returning to traffic. Specific rules may vary by state.

    Chinese Tech Giant Huawei and Subsidiaries Convicted of Sanctions Violations, Fraud, Conspiracy to Steal Trade Secrets, and Money Laundering

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A federal jury in the Eastern District of Latest York returned guilty verdicts following a three-month trial against Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd.
    • In a recent development, “No person or company is above the law,” noted Attorney General Todd Blanche.
    • “For over two decades, Huawei built its global empire on a foundation of fraud, theft, and deception,” mentioned Assistant Attorney General Tysen A.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A federal jury in the Eastern District of Latest York returned guilty verdicts following a three-month trial against Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. (Huawei) and three of its subsidiaries for violating U.S. sanctions involving Iran, lying to banks, money laundering, and stealing trade secrets from American companies. As proven at trial, Huawei and several of its subsidiaries, including Chinese subsidiary Huawei Device Co. Ltd. (Huawei Device) and U.S. subsidiaries Futurewei Technologies Inc. (Futurewei) and Huawei Device USA Inc. (Huawei Device USA), engaged in a decades-long scheme to enrich Huawei and grow its telecommunications business, including in the United States, through criminal activities.

    In a recent development, “No person or company is above the law,” noted Attorney General Todd Blanche. “For decades, Huawei and three of its subsidiaries conducted their business in the United States on the basis of lies and theft. Thanks to the work of the FBI and our federal prosecutors, those who engaged in these criminal activities will be held accountable.”.

    “For over two decades, Huawei built its global empire on a foundation of fraud, theft, and deception,” mentioned Assistant Attorney General Tysen A. Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “Huawei’s crimes threatened the U.S. financial system, took advantage of American companies that compete honestly in the global telecommunications market, and undermined our national security. Today’s verdict sends an unmistakable message: America will defend its businesses, protect its workers, and safeguard its national security against corrupt foreign corporations that lie, cheat, and steal to get ahead.”.

    “Huawei violated our laws, empowered our enemies, and harmed our national security,” noted Acting Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General for National Security M. Scott Proctor. “This conviction shows that the National Security Division and its partners will not rest until companies like Huawei are held to account for their bad conduct in an American court of justice.”.

    “Few crimes are as serious as Huawei’s decades-long pattern of endangering U.S. national security, violating the sanctity of U.S. commerce, and impeding the enforcement of U.S. laws,” remarked U.S. Attorney Joseph Nocella Jr. for the Eastern District of New York. “Today’s verdict is a step towards accountability for Huawei’s criminal activities, which includes yearslong collaboration with sanctioned entities in Iran, repeated lies to banks, and blatant thefts from U.S. technology companies.”.

    “For years, Huawei and its subsidiaries carried out an egregious campaign to expand their international enterprise through theft of trade secrets, fraud, and other criminal conduct at the expense of U.S. companies and the rule of law,” noted Assistant Director Roman Rozhavsky of the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division. “This case serves as a stark reminder that the Chinese government continues to pose a serious threat to our economic and national security, but today’s guilty verdict proves the FBI and our partners will aggressively investigate, expose, and hold accountable those who target our nation. No organization is too massive, too powerful, or too well connected to exploit the U.S. and its citizens and expect to escape American justice.”.

    Industry observers note that huawei and its subsidiaries assisted the government of the Islamic Republic of Iran by providing turnkey services with respect to an internet backbone and broader accessibility for mobile networks in the country. Huawei also helped the Iranian regime and a component of the Iranian intelligence apparatus, Zaeim, to monitor and censor its owners’ access to the internet. Testimony further established that Huawei provided surveillance cameras that enabled the Iranian regime to monitor protest activity.

    It has been revealed that huawei conducted its business in Iran under the name “Skycom.” Huawei repeatedly lied about the nature of its business in Iran, falsely telling banks, journalists, and the U.S. government that it did not assist Iran’s government, military, or intelligence community; that it began restricting its business in Iran in 2011; that Skycom was a business partner, rather than a wholly-owned subsidiary; and that Huawei complied with all applicable sanctions. Huawei knew that all of those statements were materially false and misleading.

    Huawei lied about its activities in Iran to banks to obtain billions of U.S. dollars and access to U.S.-dollar clearing services, which enabled Huawei to be a sophisticated participant in a global marketplace for telecommunications services — in part because of its lies.

    The jury convicted Huawei and three subsidiaries of conspiracy to steal trade secrets, conspiracy to commit wire and bank fraud, wire fraud, bank fraud, conspiracy to defraud the United States, conspiracy to violate the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), substantive violations of IEEPA, and money laundering conspiracy. When sentenced, the defendants face financial penalties including criminal fines, forfeiture, and restitution. Sentencing has been set for Sept. 14, 2027. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

    The investigation is being conducted by the FBI’s Upcoming York Field Office.

    Recent findings suggest that trial Attorneys Taylor G. Stout, Morgan Cohen, and Jasmin Salehi Fashemi of the Criminal Division’s Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section (MNF), Trial Attorney Aaron L. Jennen of the National Security Division’s Counterintelligence and Export Control Section, and Assistant U.S. Attorneys Alexander A. Solomon, Meredith A. Arfa, Robert M. Pollack, Matthew Skurnik, and Matthew F. Sullivan for the Eastern District of Newly introduced York (EDNY) are prosecuting the case, with assistance provided by Assistant U.S. Attorney Brendan G. King, EDNY paralegal specialists Matthew Jennings and Grace Yang, and MNF paralegal specialists Christina Roman, Alexa Stiles, Heather DePremio, Jackson Mayo, and Angela R. Ancalle Jiménez.

    Industry observers note that MNF’s mission is to take the profit out of crime, eliminate drug cartels, and protect the U.S. financial system. MNF pursues criminal prosecutions and criminal and civil asset recovery actions involving: financial facilitators who launder profits for criminals; financial institutions and their officers and employees whose actions threaten the U.S. financial system and financial institutions; international money launderers who support transnational organized crime; and the top command and control of international drug trafficking organizations.

    MNF’s Bank Integrity Unit investigates and prosecutes banks and other financial institutions, including their officers, managers and employees whose actions threaten the integrity of the individual institution or the wider financial system.

    In a recent development, at the end of the cable is a 31-millimeter self-leveling camera head. The self-leveling design keeps the image upright as the camera rotates inside the pipe, making footage easier to interpret than video that constantly spins as the cable moves.

    Salt your driveway like a pro this winter with these expert-backed tips.

    The Centers for Disease Control report a 35 percent increase in outdoor slips and falls during the winter months. Icy sidewalks, stairs and driveways are largely to blame for this seasonal uptick. Icy driveways are not only dangerous to walk on but also make driving and parking difficult. Ice melt salt is one of the best ways to keep driveways clear, but how should you best use it? Should you apply it before or after a storm — or both? Two industry experts weigh in on the best way to salt your driveway for optimal results this winter.

    Recent findings suggest that it depends. Salting before a significant storm with heavy snow and ice accumulation is a good idea, but timing matters.

    Initiative to apply salt several hours before a storm hits for best results. It creates a salty coating that prevents the initial snowfall from bonding with the driveway surface. Pre-salting reduces total snow accumulation and makes snow removal easier once the storm is over. Avoid doing it too far in advance, or if rain is in the forecast, as the salt can be washed or blown away before the snow arrives. It’s not necessary to salt before a light snowfall of less than six inches.

    It’s always a good idea to salt after it snows, but don’t rely on it to replace snow removal efforts. First remove as much snow as possible with a shovel or snowblower, then use salt to clear away any remaining slush and snow.

    The best time to salt is immediately after snow removal, before cold nighttime temperatures set in. “When applied before the temperatures drop, salt prevents ice from forming and ensures the snow does not freeze solid to the ground,” Angelika Klimorowski, a winter maintenance specialist at Online Rock Salt, claims.

    Apply salt before and after a big storm for best results, especially when heavy snow, sleet or freezing rain is expected.

    “Pre-salting helps prevent ice from bonding to the driveway, while a second application can help break down any ice that forms,” Aaron Strickland, owner of Mr. Trim Lawn & Garden Services, indicates. “For a typical snowfall, both applications usually aren’t necessary.”.

    In a recent development, if only a few inches of snow is forecast, salting after snow removal is likely sufficient. Applying salt before and after a small storm is not only a waste of money, but can damage driveway surfaces, burn lawn edges and generate harmful storm runoff.

    “The exact amount of rock salt that you need will depend on how big the area is that you are planning to de-ice,” Klimorowski states. A little goes a long way, and more is not better. A 12-oz. coffee mug filled with salt is enough to treat a 1,000-sq.-ft. driveway. Spread salt evenly, leaving about 3 inches between salt grains. Avoid overapplication, as it can degrade driveway surfaces and harm the environment.

    A handheld spreader makes application easier and more consistent, especially for larger driveways. “We try to follow recommended coverage rates and use a spreader wherever possible,” Strickland says. “Too much salt wastes product and can damage surrounding grass and gardens.” If spreading salt by hand, always wear gloves and cascade it for even coverage.

    Rock salt is only effective down to ground temperatures of 15 to 17 degrees. Don’t apply more salt if it’s not working, as it’s likely too cold out for it to work. “If your area tends to experience colder temperatures, you may need to find an alternative de-icing product to keep your surfaces safe,” Klimorowski says. Calcium chloride and magnesium chloride ice melt products are two common alternatives that remain effective at sub-zero temperatures.

    It has been revealed that yes, rain will wash away salt rather than dissolve it. It then ends up in storm drains and potentially pollutes local bodies of water.

    Rock salt stops working in temperatures below 10 to 15 degrees.

    “While it is true that salt will work best if you apply it before the temperatures drop, there is no deadline, and you can always apply it later,” Klimorowski notes.

    Sources indicate that there’s no guarantee salt will damage your driveway, but you should use it sparingly. Concrete driveways are particularly vulnerable to salt damage.

I believe this country needs deep criminal justice and police reform. I am galled by ICE agents ethnically profiling and brutalizing people. I not only support gay marriage but am an enthusiastic participant in one.

    In a recent development, but wokeness is not about a basic concern for social justice. It hyperfocuses on language and identity, fights dirty from the moral high ground and mandates deference to self-appointed spokespeople for marginalized groups. It conflates disagreement with harm, and keeps careful watch for heretics.

At its worst, the energy reminds me of a scene from an Oberlin dining co-op, where a group of members filed in during a meal and silently unfurled a sign reading, "This co-op is messed up."     Recent findings suggest that as for wokeness, I suspect that many progressive elected officials are privately rankled by its excesses, but publicly inclined to ignore it, worried about inviting moral hectoring from the left. The most productive thing they can do now is grow a backbone. They need to take it upon themselves to elevate the best, most compelling ideas even when doing so earns them some pushback.

    Industry observers note that day's arguments, including her suggestion that DSA types should embrace "carceral minimalism" instead of prison abolition--what she calls a "nonsensical position"--is facing pushback from the Left.     Tech Report: How to Shovel the Trickiest Surfaces the Right Way, From Pavers to Your Roof

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • From lawns to sealed concrete, you might be surprised at how much damage a snow shovel can do.
    • Recent findings suggest that clearing snow from walkways is vital for safety, but winter shoveling can easily damage wooden decks, asphalt driveways and other surfaces.
    • In a recent development, “Snow can camouflage uneven areas and patches of ice, posing slip-and-fall risks, particularly when you’re rushing to shovel,” says landscaping expert Jose Lopez.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Family Handyman's Editorial Process.

    From lawns to sealed concrete, you might be surprised at how much damage a snow shovel can do.

    Recent findings suggest that clearing snow from walkways is vital for safety, but winter shoveling can easily damage wooden decks, asphalt driveways and other surfaces. So, as the days get shorter and colder, it’s important to solidify your shoveling plan before the first snow flies.

    In a recent development, “Snow can camouflage uneven areas and patches of ice, posing slip-and-fall risks, particularly when you’re rushing to shovel,” says landscaping expert Jose Lopez. “Being mindful and taking a relaxed, careful approach will help you save money and keep everyone safe all winter long.”.

    Ahead, experts walk through how to shovel eleven tricky surfaces around your home, to keep everyone safe, plus prevent costly springtime repairs.

    It has been revealed that shoveling gravel is frustrating because those pebbles tend to come up with the snow, then get scattered onto the landscaping. “You will end up cleaning about $150 worth of it off your lawn in the spring,” notes grading and paving contractor Scott Flores.

    To make life easier, use a plastic shovel, keep the blade about an inch above the gravel and clear the snow in short passes. “You don’t have to expose all of the gravel,” says Lopez. “It’s fine to leave a thin layer of snow behind.”.

    In a recent development, A metal snow shovel blade can actually scratch and gouge concrete. “It can cause $3,000 worth of damage to your pavement in 20 minutes and you won’t know it ’til April,” states Flores. Initially, the damage “may not look like much, but once water gets under it and freezes, it will cause spalling and make your pavement look 10 years older than it is.”.

    Luckily, the fix is easy on this one: always use a poly-blade (plastic) or rubber-edged shovel on concrete.

    Aliaksandr Bahdanovich/Getty Images.

    Aggressive shoveling can damage paint and sealers, even if they’re touted as “scratch-resistant.” “That layer is about three millimeters thick, and your steel shovel will chip it away like you’re peeling your fingernails,” indicates Flores.

    The fix: use a poly-blade shovel, shovel with a slight upward motion and leave a half-inch of snow for the sun to melt, says Flores. “Many believe that steel shovels will last longer. Yes they will, but that’s what makes them bad,” he says.

    Pro-tip: If you use a deicer, make sure it’s safe for your particular coating, says Lopez.

    Just like with concrete, asphalt seems indestructible, but metal shovels can damage it, especially if it already has imperfections or cracks. So, the best approach is to use a poly-blade (plastic) or rubber-edged shovel, and shovel the snow before it partially melts and refreezes.

    Industry observers note that “Avoid pushing your shovel into cracks or potholes, and don’t bang it against the surface in an attempt to dislodge stubborn ice,” claims Lopez. “Instead, choose a deicing product that’s safe for asphalt.”.

    It has been revealed that A shovel can easily catch the edge of a paver and scratch, break or knock it out of place. To prevent that, use a poly-blade shovel, take shorter shovel strokes, push snow at an angle and slightly raise up the leading edge.

    Industry observers note that “Shoveling and deicing aggressively won’t make your job faster or easier, it takes some finesse,” states Lopez. Also, use de-icers that are safe for both the paving and jointing material, and inspect the walkway for loose bricks once the snow melts.

    According to recent reports, after a snow, it can be tricky to tell where the concrete ends and the lawn begins, and one wrong move means damaged grass come springtime. To keep from marring your grass, mark walkway edges with small flags before it snows. While shoveling, keep the blade even with your walkway, versus angling it toward the grass.

    Pro-tip: “Slow down and work in short passes near the edges, rather than trying to force the shovel along,” notes Lopez. “.

    It has been revealed that try not to pile snow on shrubs and other perennials, as that can snap branches. It’s also best to keep deicers and their runoff away from landscaping.

    Sources indicate that “Before winter arrives, proposal where you’ll pile or toss snow to keep it away from sensitive plants,” claims Lopez. “You may find it helpful to use a smaller shovel, which will give you better control over where the snow lands.”.

    In a recent development, also, try not to move soil, which can expose plants to the cold, and never strike frozen branches to remove snow. “Wood breaks more easily than people expect,” states moving professional Leon Schwab.

    Industry observers note that aggressive shoveling is sure to damage a deck, regardless of its composition. To preserve yours, use a poly-blade shovel and push the snow in the direction of the boards. If it’s safe to do so, leave a thin layer of snow, instead of shoveling all the way down to bare decking, then apply a deicer that’s recommended for the surface type.

    Industry observers note that safety tip: “If wet, heavy snow is accumulating and you notice the deck sagging or hear creaking noises, seek professional advice,” says Lopez. “Don’t continue using the deck if you suspect a structural issue.”.

    Stairs are particularly hazardous when its slippery out, and clearing them can be precarious, with snow obscuring their boundaries and confined spaces limiting your range of motion.

    To stay safe, “Wear boots with good traction and make sure your staircase is well lit,” says Lopez. “Don’t rush the job. It’s better to take your time and shovel safely.”.

    Pro-tip: “Use a small shovel to clear one step at a time and maintain a stable position,” states Schwab.

    Sometimes it’s prudent to clear large accumulations of snow from the roof, but it’s also a dangerous job. To stay safe, roofing contractor Andre Kazimierski recommends using a roof rake, which allows you to pull off snow while remaining on the ground. Focus on clearing off as much as you can, but don’t worry about leaving it completely bare, and try not to touch your roofing material.

    “Do this sooner rather than later, because if it starts to warm up a bit the snow will become denser and heavier, making it harder to remove,” notes Kazimierski. “And never walk on your roof when it’s even the slightest bit snowy or icy up there.”.

    Recent findings suggest that obviously, you don’t want to take a shovel to your car, as that would do a lot of damage. Instead, use a snow brush or broom that’s designed to be gentle on vehicle finishes. Flores recommends this one from Snow Joe.

    Recent findings suggest that start by clearing the roof in sections, then move on to the hood, trunk, windows, headlights, taillights and mirrors. You’ll especially want to get the roof and hood fully clear; otherwise, once you start driving, snow can blow up or slide down onto your windshield, obstructing your vision and endangering other drivers. “That ice can fly off your car at 40 miles per hour,” says Flores.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that today, the Justice Department confirmed the results of a historic surge in resources to protect Americans from criminal scam networks and online fraud following President Trump’s Executive Order 14390 directing a government-wide crackdown. Since the Executive Order was signed on March 6, Justice Department prosecutors have taken action to protect Americans in over 400 cases against over 800 defendants.

    These actions include newly introduced charges, extraditions, guilty verdicts, and criminal sentences. U.S. prosecutors and agents also assisted law enforcement in over 10 countries in raids of foreign scam call centers and compounds that targeted Americans.

    “Predatory scams against the American people will not be tolerated,” noted Attorney General Todd Blanche. “The unprecedented results of this surge are just the beginning. We will continue prosecuting those who perpetrate these schemes and disrupting the activities of transnational criminal organizations before they reach American shores.”.

    Sources indicate that “Under President Trump’s Executive Order 14390, this FBI has made dismantling predatory scam enterprises a top priority using a whole-of-government approach,” remarked FBI Director Kash Patel. “Through Operation Blackout, this FBI’s scam center demolition initiative, we’ve seized nearly $17 billion in illicit funds, taken more than 14,000 digital devices, directly warned over 11,000 Americans from scam attempts, and prevented more than $690 million in potential victim losses. The Trump Administration is crushing scam centers plaguing Americans, and with Attorney General Blanche and our interagency partners, we are delivering on this righteous mission every day all over the world. The message to these scam syndicates is clear: if you target Americans, justice will find you.”.

    According to recent reports, “Scammers worldwide steal billions of dollars from Americans each year, profiting from lies and vulnerability,” noted Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “Under President Trump and Attorney General Blanche, the Criminal Division is taking the fight directly to the criminal networks that are stealing from Americans. We will not allow these scammers to hide behind their screens or escape justice by committing these crimes abroad. The Justice Department will use every tool at its disposal to disrupt predatory schemes, punish wrongdoers, and protect the American people.”.

    It has been revealed that according to Gallup, 10% of U.S. adults experienced a scam last year, either directly or through someone in their household. Nearly three in four scam victims experienced a negative effect on their mental health or well-being. Gallup also reports that Americans lost an estimated $68 billion to scams in 2025 alone. These scams include cryptocurrency investment scams, financially motivated sextortion, government imposter schemes, and other predatory schemes that collectively cost Americans billions of dollars, with many families losing their life savings.

    In one scam charged this month, current and former members of prison gangs in Georgia used contraband mobile phones to falsely tell victims that they missed jury duty and would be arrested if they failed to pay a “fine.” 14 individuals were charged in three indictments in federal and state courts for participation in these schemes, and another 17 defendants were charged in state court for a scheme to smuggle contraband mobile phones, often used to perpetrate fraud schemes and other crimes, into Georgia prisons. Websites that were used by inmates to commit jury duty imposter schemes were seized. Below are social media posts by Georgia prison inmates flaunting the proceeds of fraud schemes and contraband mobile phones used to contact victims.

    Industry observers note that the anti-scam surge was coordinated by the Justice Department's Criminal Division, which brought together a dedicated team of prosecutors to identify scammers, disrupt their networks, and hold them accountable. This team includes experts across the Criminal Division’s sections, including the White Collar and Corporate Enforcement Section, Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section, Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section, Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Human Rights and Special Prosecutions Section, Office of Overseas Prosecutorial Development, Assistance and Training, and the Office of International Affairs.

    It has been revealed that the whole-of-government approach includes initiatives by the FBI, State Department, Department of Homeland Security, including Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) and U.S. Secret Service, Treasury Department, U.S. Postal Inspection Service (USPIS), Federal Communications Commission, Federal Trade Commission (FTC), Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, and Internal Revenue Service (IRS).

    During the surge period from March 6 to present, Assistant U.S. Attorneys and Criminal Division trial attorneys contributed to the surge by obtaining wide-ranging results in 85 federal districts across the country. 30 defendants were extradited to face scam-related charges in U.S. courts.     The Justice Department coordinated with other agencies to launch a public education and messaging campaign informing consumers of the dangers of fraud, providing guidance on avoiding schemes, and encouraging Americans to use the upcoming holiday season to “Share Your Scam Story” with friends and relatives.

    Operation Blackout is the FBI’s global counter-scam demolition initiative. Through intelligence-driven operations and close collaboration with international law enforcement and government partners, the FBI has restrained nearly $17 billion in illicit funds, seized more than 14,000 digital devices, and helped identify, disrupt, and dismantle over 29 scam compounds operating across Asia, Africa, and the Middle East. These operations resulted in the federal charging of more than 50 scam actors, while FBI coordination and investigative support enabled foreign partners to arrest or detain more than 320 additional perpetrators overseas.

    Industry observers note that working alongside international partners, the FBI also assisted in the liberation and repatriation of more than 2,200 trafficked workers forced to operate inside scam compounds. Since Executive Order 14390 on March 6th, Operation Level Up has prevented more than $143 million in victim losses, warned thousands of Americans they were being targeted by a scammer and frozen over $350 million in assets through FBI’s Recovery Asset Team.

    Industry observers note that as part of this coordinated global effort, the State Department funds U.S. law enforcement advisors who train and mentor foreign investigators and prosecutors to work on U.S. cases. In Southeast Asia, advisors mentor and provide technical assistance to local law enforcement on scam investigations. To date, the State Department funded and supported U.S. and Southeast Asian law enforcement to facilitate the freezing of more than $1 billion in stolen cryptocurrency, the takedown of over 1.4 million fraudulent websites and accounts, numerous arrests, and several pending extraditions. State Department-funded forensic tools helped analyze more than 10,000 devices and hard drives in Thailand alone, allowing U.S. and Thai law enforcement to better understand the criminal networks and advance U.S. investigations.

    In Moldova, the State Department trained local prosecutors who oversaw the October arrests of three suspects in an online romance scheme that took $440,000 from American and European victims in a single month. Additionally, the State Department provided investigative training, protective equipment, and forensics software that enabled raids in October that resulted in the closure of five call centers and detained eight suspected coordinators who allegedly ran fake cryptocurrency trading platforms that defrauded investors.

    Recent findings suggest that "Too many Americans have suffered from cyber fraud, particularly from scam operations emanating from Southeast Asia, and expanding across South Asia, the Middle East, Africa, and the Pacific. But the true cost is not in dollars alone. Behind every statistic is a human story – a family bankrupted, a retiree left destitute, or a young person driven to suicide," mentioned Deputy Assistant Secretary of State David Bedard. "We know the threat is evolving, and we are prepared to develop new tools and strategies to prevent scammers and other criminals from stealing from and harming Americans. Cyber-enabled fraud is proliferating around the world, so we must stay vigilant and build partnerships to combat it.".

    Homeland Security Investigations.

    Since March 6, HSI offices nationwide executed more than 300 arrests, worked with the Justice Department to indict more than 100 defendants, and secured approximately 80 convictions and guilty pleas. HSI’s financial fraud investigations have also resulted in the seizure, restraint, freezing, or recovery of more than $120 million dollars in illicit proceeds, including funds held in bank and cryptocurrency accounts, cash, precious metals, vehicles, real property, and other assets. HSI works with domestic and international law enforcement partners, prosecutors, financial institutions, and private-sector stakeholders to identify and dismantle the criminal networks responsible, trace and recover illicit proceeds, and pursue the return of funds to victims when legally authorized.

    Recent findings suggest that “HSI is committed to identifying and dismantling the criminal networks that perpetrate these crimes, wherever they operate, while tracing and seizing illicit proceeds and pursuing the return of funds to victims whenever legally authorized,” noted HSI Acting Executive Associate Director John A. Condon. “Through close coordination with our domestic and international law enforcement partners, prosecutors, financial institutions, and private-sector stakeholders, HSI will continue to hold these actors accountable and protect the American public from evolving financial threats.”.

    During the surge period, Secret Service investigators have restrained more than $200 million in illicit funds, disrupted 1,780 domains operated by scammers, and recovered more than $119 million while investigating more than 1,540 business email compromise incidents. Secret Service-led cases included the identification of a cryptocurrency investment conspiracy operated from scam centers in Cambodia that targeted at least 174 U.S. victims. In October, a Chinese national was extradited from the Netherlands and arraigned in the Central District of California for his alleged role in that conspiracy.

    Recent findings suggest that “While we are encouraged by the progress made to date, our investigators continue to lead dozens of cases involving transnational criminal networks targeting the American people,” stated U.S. Secret Service Director Sean Curran. “Today’s announcement demonstrates that scammers operating anywhere in the world can be identified and brought to justice. The Secret Service remains committed to its founding mission of investigating financial crimes and will continue to work with law enforcement partners in the United States and around the world to dismantle and disrupt these criminal networks.”.

    During the surge period, USPIS supported cases against dozens of defendants, including those who perpetrated jury duty imposter schemes described above, lottery and sweepstakes fraud, inheritance fraud, and fraud against Spanish-speaking Americans. Several of these cases involved prosecutions of list brokers who knowingly provided the names of elderly Americans to fraudsters operating abroad. USPIS also seized three internet domains linked to jury duty imposter schemes perpetrated by Georgia prison inmates. Traffic to all three web addresses was redirected to official government servers displaying a public seizure banner. This coordinated takedown effectively dismantled the operators’ digital infrastructure and prevented further public victimization. USPIS also partnered with the Justice Department to mail out over 4,800 unlicensed money transmitter letters since March, which has had an incredible impact on the rates of reducing recidivism for “money mules.”.

    “Behind every scam is a person whose financial security, trust, and peace of mind have been threatened,” mentioned Chief Inspector Gary Barksdale. “The Postal Inspection Service brings investigative expertise, nationwide reach, and a longstanding commitment to protecting consumers to this effort. Together with the Department of Justice and our partners, the USPIS is working to disrupt these criminal networks, pursue accountability, and prevent others from becoming victims.”.

    It has been revealed that during the surge period, the FTC filed 16 actions challenging deceptive earnings claims, unfair payment processing practices, tech support scams, debt relief schemes, unauthorized billing practices, misleading claims about health products, health insurance frauds, government and business impersonations, and deceptive claims about sextortion assistance services. The FTC has continued to work with domain registrars and others to take down social media pages and 19 websites impersonating the FTC or FTC officials. Since April 2026, the FTC has connected more than 365 callers to the Justice Department’s National Elder Fraud Hotline and provided the hotline number to more than 7,100 online filers.

    Sources indicate that “The FTC has been on the front lines of tackling fraud for more than a century,” mentioned FTC Chairman and Anti-Fraud Task Force Vice Chairman Andrew N. Ferguson. “Thanks to President Trump’s comprehensive, government-wide approach to stopping fraud, the Trump FTC has returned almost $3 billion to American consumers who have been harmed by fraud and deception. The Trump Administration’s message to the bad actors who lie, cheat and steal to defraud Americans out of their hard-earned money is clear: you are living on borrowed time. The FTC is proud to work alongside its federal partners to protect Americans from scammers, whether the crooks are here at home or abroad.”.

    Securities and Exchange Commission.

    Since March 2026, the SEC has filed enforcement actions against 39 entities for allegedly filing false Forms ADV to create the appearance of legitimate U.S. investment advisers and lure retail investors and charged multiple entities with fraud in connection with so-called investment confidence scams that feigned SEC compliance while misappropriating more than $15 million from investors through online platforms. In the last year, the SEC also charged three purported crypto asset trading platforms and four investment clubs with allegedly defrauding retail investors of more than $14 million through an online investment-confidence scam. The SEC charged BG Wealth Sharing Ltd and DSJ Exchange Pty Ltd with an alleged investment fraud scheme that raised more than $130 million from tens of thousands of retail investors across the U.S. and abroad. The SEC has issued investor alerts warning investors that fraudsters may use social media platforms and messaging apps or claim to be officially registered with the SEC to lure investors into scams. The SEC also encourages investors to visit Investor.gov to verify the background of individuals offering investment opportunities.

    Industry observers note that “Advances in technology have lowered the barriers to entry for fraudsters, making it easier to reach potential victims and making fraudulent schemes appear more legitimate,” noted David Woodcock, Director of the SEC's Division of Enforcement. “The technology may be new, but the frauds are familiar. We will continue working with our law enforcement partners to target these schemes and hold those responsible accountable.”.

    Federal Communications Commission.

    On Nov. 19, the FCC approved a fresh rule to allow federal and state prisons and jails to use jamming technology to block calls from illegal contraband cell phones that can be used to coordinate outside illegal activity, including the jury duty scams described above as well as scams explicitly targeting U.S. veterans. The FCC has also taken concrete actions to target scammers and illegal robocallers. The FCC has stopped nearly 300 million illegal robocalls, saving Americans at least $38 million through enforcement and reforms that led to the blocking of more than 1,400 providers and 296 million illegal robocalls.
